modal.subtitle: Plain-language explanations for beginners alongside technical specifications for system engineers.

proxy.simple: An intermediary relay server. Websites see the proxy server's IP address and location instead of yours.
proxy.expert: L4/L7 transport tunnel supporting TCP relay, RFC 1928 UDP Associate, and HTTP CONNECT.

chain.simple: Routes your traffic through multiple proxies in a row for extra privacy, or automatically switches to a backup proxy if one goes down.
chain.expert: Sequential multi-hop tunneling (Entry -> Exit), high-availability failover, or automatic lowest-RTT node selection.

fake_ip.simple: Prevents your Internet provider from spying on which websites you visit by assigning a temporary virtual IP to every domain.
fake_ip.expert: Bidirectional in-memory RFC 2544 allocator that intercepts DNS queries and recovers exact FQDNs on raw TCP/UDP socket connections.

killswitch.simple: A safety lock that immediately blocks an app's Internet access if the proxy disconnects, so your real IP is never exposed.
killswitch.expert: Strict DROP enforcement when the target upstream node fails or when UDP datagrams hit a TCP-only upstream proxy.

rules.simple: Your custom traffic laws: e.g., 'Firefox goes through Proxy', 'Steam connects Directly', and 'Windows Telemetry is Blocked'.
rules.expert: Deterministic ascending-priority evaluator matching process globs, domain wildcards, IPv4/IPv6 CIDR subnets, and port ranges.

system_proxy.simple: 'System Proxy' configures all of Windows in 1 click. 'Run App via Proxy' launches a single chosen program inside the proxy tunnel.
system_proxy.expert: Toggles HKCU Internet Settings registry keys or spawns a child process with injected ALL_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY environment variables.
